steps: Confirm the additional language is enabled and agree on questions and approved terminology with a fluent reviewer.
Create a concierge for that language in the same sandbox, reuse the approved source and review its opening prompts.
Run the agreed questions, correct wording or settings with the reviewer, and record the approved responses and remaining exceptions.
deliverables: Localized prompts and signed test results
asks: One enabled language and access to the existing concierge
A reviewer who can approve localized terms and answers
risk: A fluent answer can still use the wrong local terminology. Have your language reviewer sign off realistic questions and product names.
outcome: Visitors can use the approved language experience, and your team has a tested question set for future changes.

steps: Choose the product card layout and map your catalog fields to the supplied spreadsheet template.
Validate the supplied product images and links, upload the completed spreadsheet, and check processing finishes successfully.
Ask sample product questions and check each returned card leads to its intended product page.
deliverables: Mapped product spreadsheet and configured knowledge source
Sample product cards and destination link test results
asks: A small product catalog outside Adobe Commerce
Approved images, product details and destination links
risk: An outdated link can send a shopper to the wrong item. Test a sample of product cards against your approved catalog.
outcome: Visitors can open product pages from the concierge, and your team has a spreadsheet it can maintain.

steps: Agree on the events, allowed fields, consent behavior and destination with your analytics owner.
Map each supported callback into the existing collection route and forward the approved fields.
Trigger each event on a test page and compare browser activity with the receiving system, including checks for duplicate events.
asks: Access to the existing analytics destination and test page
An approved list of events and permitted fields
risk: Callbacks can carry visitor-entered text or duplicate an existing event. Limit the fields sent and reconcile test events with the receiving system.
outcome: Your analytics team can count the agreed concierge interactions alongside the website events it already measures.

steps: Agree which chat components need different styling and collect approved designs for desktop and phone.
Configure the selected components and provide a preview for your brand and website owners.
Test the agreed interaction states at both screen sizes and capture the approved settings for handover.
asks: Approved visual design and component list
Brand and website reviewers for sign-off
risk: A layout that works on a large screen can hide a control on a phone. Test both sizes with the same visitor tasks.
outcome: Visitors see the agreed branded chat controls, and your team can reproduce the approved design.

steps: Agree on the reporting period and record the baseline figures for the live concierge.
Compare conversation volume, unique users, sentiment and engagement with the prior period and flag changes for discussion.
Review the trends with your team, agree on one improvement to test and record what to compare next month.
asks: Access to the concierge dashboard and a comparable period
A business owner to agree on the next improvement
risk: A traffic spike can look like a change in visitor behavior. Compare volumes and rates together and record known changes to the site.
outcome: Your team can see changes in visitor engagement and choose a specific improvement to test next.

steps: Confirm your users belong to the organization and identify the sandboxes each operating team is approved to manage.
Configure the roles with Manage Brand Concierge permission and assign approved users to the appropriate roles.
Test representative accounts in their assigned sandboxes and verify a restricted sandbox stays inaccessible.
asks: An administrator and representative test accounts
Approved team roster and sandbox assignments
risk: A role can expose another team's sandbox. Compare each assignment against the approved roster and test permitted and restricted access.
outcome: The operating teams can manage their assigned concierges, and the administrator can verify who has access.
